roles.title: Rules for everyone
roles.summary: Do your part. The NHVR says safety of transport activities is the shared responsibility of each party in the chain. The duty cannot be handed to someone else.
roles.law: Each party in the chain has a primary duty, under section 26C, to ensure the safety of their transport activities so far as is reasonably practicable. That means removing a public risk where you can, and cutting it down where you cannot remove it. You must not cause or encourage a driver, or anyone else, to speed or to break the Heavy Vehicle National Law. The duty cannot be handed to someone else. Driving by itself does not make a driver a party in the chain, but a driver still has their own duties, including not driving while impaired by fatigue or unfit. From 1 August 2026 the Heavy Vehicle National Law changed. The NHVR flyer lists a new Heavy Vehicle Accreditation scheme, updates to fatigue requirements, simpler work diary record-keeping, and changes to mass, dimension and loading. General Mass Limits are increased to align with the Concessional Mass Limits that applied before. From 1 August 2026, the general-access length for certain combinations, including a prime mover and semitrailer, moved from 19 metres to 20 metres if the extra conditions are met. It does not apply to every vehicle, and B-doubles are not included. A rigid truck on its own stays 12.5 metres. Whether any of our combinations may run at that length is a gap. Check with your manager. Do not guess a length. A new unfit-to-drive duty applies to drivers of heavy vehicles over 4.5 tonnes. A driver whose health or fitness means they cannot drive safely must be able to stop, or not start. Work and rest hours, and work diaries, apply when the vehicle is fatigue-regulated. The NHVR describes that as a GVM over 12 tonnes, or a combination whose GVM or GCM total is over 12 tonnes. That 12 tonne figure is the NHVR’s description. It is not quoted here as a line from the Law itself. National Heavy Vehicle Accreditation Scheme entry is being progressively replaced by Heavy Vehicle Accreditation. That scheme has General Safety Accreditation and Alternative Compliance Accreditation. An operator’s Safety Management System sits at the centre of it. Whether Monaro’s accreditation changes your job is a gap. Check with your manager. Maximum court penalties in this app are from the NHVR schedule for 1 August 2026 to 30 June 2027. The NHVR indexes penalties on 1 July each year. A maximum is the most a court can impose. It is not the amount on every notice.

Do not treat the Master Code as the law. The NHVR says the 2026 Master Code does not create new legal obligations. A court may use it as evidence of what was known and of what was reasonably practicable. There is no offence for failing to use one control in the Code.

roles.title: General Manager
roles.summary: You lead the business that employs the drivers and directs the trucks.
roles.law: If you are an executive of a business that is a party in the chain — including a director, a manager, or another person who takes part in the management of the business — you must exercise due diligence to make sure the business meets its primary duty. The Heavy Vehicle National Law puts that duty in section 26D, and section 26D(1A) for an executive of a party that is not a legal entity. Due diligence means: keep your knowledge of safe heavy vehicle transport up to date; understand the hazards in our work; make sure the business has, and actually uses, the people, time and processes to remove or cut those risks; and make sure information about hazards, risks and incidents is received, considered and acted on quickly. The duty cannot be transferred. Accreditation is not required of every operator, but the primary duty still applies. The 1 August 2026 changes also cover Euro VI road-train steer-axle concessions and tag-trailer tow-mass rules. Those are not typical of this fleet of heavy rigids and semi-trailers. Check with your manager only if a combination like that is ever used. The schedule for 1 August 2026 to 30 June 2027 sets executive duty section 26D(1A) at the maximum for the matching Category 1, 2, or 3 offence by an individual. Category 1, section 26F: an individual, $436,850 or 5 years’ imprisonment or both; a corporation, $4,230,550. Category 2, section 26G: an individual, $212,090; a corporation, $2,120,880. Category 3, section 26H: an individual, $70,580; a corporation, $705,820. The schedule does not list an infringement penalty for those primary duty offences. Heavy Vehicle Accreditation is progressively replacing the National Heavy Vehicle Accreditation Scheme from 1 August 2026. Operators need a Safety Management System. Whether we are in that transition is a gap.

topics.title: What changed on 1 August 2026
topics.summary: The amended Heavy Vehicle National Law started on 1 August 2026 in the participating jurisdictions. Western Australia and the Northern Territory are not participating jurisdictions. This card is the short list. The topic pages have the tables.
topics.law: Checked on 23 Nov 2026 against the NHVR work-and-rest page, the General Mass Limits page, the general access page, the mass and dimension fact sheet dated 5 August 2026, and the penalty schedule for 1 August 2026 to 30 June 2027. A driver must not drive a heavy vehicle over 4.5 tonnes while impaired by fatigue or unfit, even inside the hours. General Mass Limits now include 17.0 tonnes on a non-pig tandem with dual tyres and 21.0 tonnes on a non-pig tri-axle with dual tyres or wide singles. Certain combinations, including a prime mover and one semitrailer, may be up to 20 metres if the stated conditions are met. Mass accreditation is not required just to use those former Concessional Mass Limit masses. Existing BFM or AFM accreditation may continue until it expires, is cancelled, or the operator moves to Heavy Vehicle Accreditation. New applicants use Alternative Compliance Hours, not a new BFM or AFM module. Penalty maximums in this app are from the schedule for 1 August 2026 to 30 June 2027.

topics.title: Fatigue and fitness
topics.summary: Standard Hours are the default for a solo driver in a truck. You can still be unfit inside those hours. Which option Monaro Milk uses has not been confirmed. Check with the office before you use any other numbers.
topics.law: From 1 August 2026 a driver must not drive any heavy vehicle over 4.5 tonnes GVM while impaired by fatigue or unfit to drive, even inside the work and rest limits. Parties must not cause or encourage a driver to exceed the limits, and drivers must be able to stop. Standard Hours need no accreditation. You operate under one option at a time: Standard Hours, BFM, AFM, Alternative Compliance Hours, or an exemption. BFM and AFM were NHVAS modules. An operator who still holds that accreditation may keep using it until it expires, is cancelled, or they move to Heavy Vehicle Accreditation. The NHVR page does not give every certificate a blanket three-year window. AFM hours are the ones printed on that operator’s certificate, which the driver must carry. Alternative Compliance Hours are printed on an ACA–Fatigue certificate. Drivers cannot choose those hours themselves. Monaro Milk’s option is not confirmed in this app.

Do not run two hours options on the same day to make more time. A change of option has its own reset rules, including a 48-hour continuous rest in the cases the NHVR sets out.

topics.title: Work diary
topics.summary: Logmaster is the electronic work diary Monaro Milk uses. A written National Driver Work Diary is the paper alternative. Whether Logmaster is the NHVR-approved device for this operator was not re-checked on an approved-device list in this run. If you are unsure what to enter, check with the office.
topics.law: Under Standard Hours you must use a work diary when you will work more than 100 km from your base. You must also carry it if you did 100 km-plus Standard Hours work in the last 28 days. Under BFM, AFM, Alternative Compliance Hours or exemption hours you must use a work diary at any distance, and you must carry it if you worked under one of those options in the last 28 days. Inside 100 km on Standard Hours you still complete a local area record. The record keeper keeps fatigue records for three years. A written work diary can be bought for $31. From 1 August 2026 some daily-sheet fields on the written diary, including marking the day of the week and marking Standard Hours, are optional. Our drivers record in Logmaster. What Logmaster requires you to enter is a gap if the office has not told you.

cards.text: On a 100 km-plus Standard Hours day, record the whole day in the work diary, from the start of the day, not only the part after you realised the trip was long.

For local Standard Hours work, record the date, each truck’s registration, and your work and rest totals for the day and the week. Finish the local record within 24 hours of stopping work that day, and give it to the record keeper within 21 days.

If Logmaster fails, is full, or is lost, stolen or destroyed, tell your record keeper within two business days and use the supplementary record they direct. The record keeper notifies the NHVR within two business days. Do not invent the missing hours.

If a written work diary is full, lost, stolen or destroyed, notify the NHVR within two business days. Use a supplementary record for at most seven business days. Keep a copy in the vehicle for 28 days, and give a copy to the record keeper within 21 days.

Work is every task to do with operating the fatigue-regulated heavy vehicle, including on private property. Rest is any time that is not work. In a written work diary, work rounds up to the next 15 minutes and rest rounds down to the previous 15 minutes. In an electronic work diary, work and rest are counted in whole minutes, and a continuous rest shorter than 15 minutes does not count toward a minimum rest.

topics.title: Load restraint in hard-sided bodies
topics.summary: Every body we run is a hard-sided refrigerated or pantech body. There are no tankers and no bulk liquid. Shutting the doors does not, by itself, restrain the load. Whether these sides are rated was not verified. If the rating is unknown, do not rely on the walls alone.
topics.law: Being inside a hard-sided refrigerated body is not, by itself, a restrained load. Schedule 7 of the Mass, Dimension and Loading Regulation, as the NHVR performance-standards page states it, requires a restraint system that can withstand 0.8 g forwards (80% of the weight of the load), 0.5 g sideways and 0.5 g rearwards, and 0.2 g upwards if the system relies on friction. The structure has to be strong enough, and the load must not be able to build up speed through a gap. Whether these bodies have a known rating is a gap. Check with your manager. The Load Restraint Guide 2018 is guidance for meeting those standards. The NHVR says the 2018 guide remains valid; the 2025 edition is a rebrand with minor changes, not a new law. For general freight the 2018 guide says a cumulative gap of up to 200 mm front to back and up to 100 mm side to side is acceptable, and that larger gaps let freight move. Pack contained loads tight. Fill gaps with empty pallets or other suitable blocking. Do not use rope on a heavy load. Rope does not have the lashing capacity.

cards.text: Unitise the crates to the pallet, then block the pallet to the headboard and the sides, or fill the gaps. Unitising alone is not restraint.

If you are the loader, tell the driver what is on the truck. If you are the driver, do not leave until you are satisfied the pallets will stay put.

Do not assume the load is restrained just because the doors are shut. Enclosed does not equal restrained. The structure must resist 0.8 g forwards and 0.5 g sideways and rearwards, and the load must not build up speed in a gap. If the rating is unknown, use extra restraint.
Do not leave a cumulative gap over 200 mm front to back or over 100 mm side to side without extra blocking or lashings.

topics.law: Section 26C is the primary duty: each party must ensure, so far as is reasonably practicable, the safety of that party’s transport activities. That includes eliminating or minimising public risks, and not causing or encouraging the driver to break the law or to speed. Section 26D is executive due diligence. From 1 August 2026, section 26D(1A) is the due-diligence duty for the primary duty, and the maximum is the matching Category 1, 2 or 3 maximum for an individual. Section 26E is prohibited requests and contracts, not the due-diligence section. The Master Code is evidence of what is reasonably practicable. It is not the law, and there is no offence for missing one control in it. For this business the functions that come up are employer, operator, scheduler, consignor, consignee, packer, loading manager, loader and unloader. topics.title: Interstate, NSW and Victoria
topics.summary: The owner has confirmed these interstate runs are New South Wales and Victoria. Both are Heavy Vehicle National Law jurisdictions. The law does not apply in Western Australia or the Northern Territory. This page does not set a Victorian curfew.
topics.law: Crossing from New South Wales into Victoria does not reset your work and rest count and does not switch off mass or loading rules. A New South Wales route, mass or PBS approval does not automatically apply in Victoria, and a Victorian approval does not automatically apply in New South Wales. A PBS approval or a notice in one state does not by itself authorise every road in the other. Higher general-access mass or length does not automatically open every local road. quiz.prompt: You are asked to finish the load during the driver’s rest. What do you do?
choices: Stop and tell your manager
Finish it so the product stays cold
Finish it if you can do it in five minutes
quiz.why: Do not use the rest break. Tell your manager. They can change the plan. Cold product does not make a rest break into loading time. Stop and tell your manager.

quiz.prompt: You do not know whether this hard-sided body is rated for the pallets. What do you do?
choices: Check with your manager before you keep stacking, and do not rely on the walls alone
Stack it the way you did last year
Fill the body until nothing moves by eye
quiz.why: The Load Restraint Guide 2018 and the NHVR say containment counts when the structure is strong enough and the gaps are controlled. A rating we have not seen is a gap. Check with your manager.

quiz.prompt: Putting goods on the heavy vehicle means you are:
choices: A loader, for that task
Outside the chain, because you are on a forklift
The driver
quiz.why: Loading the heavy vehicle is the loader function, whatever machine you use to do it. If you put the freight on the truck, you are a loader for that task.

quiz.prompt: The truck is not safe to leave. What do you do?
choices: Keep it stopped and tell the General Manager
Let it go if the run is short
Tell the driver to be careful
quiz.why: Keep it stopped and tell the General Manager. A short run is still a trip on the road. Keep it stopped and tell the General Manager.

choices: Goes to the General Manager. Do not delete it

Is only the driver’s concern

Yes. Every workshop in Australia was enrolled that day
Yes, but only for local runs

quiz.prompt: Someone asks you to change a record so the day looks legal. What do you do?
choices: Do not change it. Tell your manager
Change it if they are senior to you
Delete the day
quiz.why: Keep the true record. Tell your manager. Do not change it and do not delete the day, whoever asks. Tell your manager.

quiz.prompt: Booking a delivery time can mean you are:
choices: Helping to schedule or consign. The time must be achievable without speeding or skipped rest
Outside the chain, because you are in the office
The driver for that day
quiz.why: The function decides it. A time you book can push the driver. Make it achievable, or check with your manager. Office work can still be scheduling or consigning. The time has to be achievable safely.

quiz.prompt: You are not sure a task is a Chain of Responsibility function. What do you do?
choices: Check with your manager
Ignore it if the word is not in your contract
Decide it is not your job
quiz.why: The NHVR says the function decides it, not the contract wording. If you are unsure, check with your manager. The contract does not decide it. Check with your manager.

quiz.prompt: PBS, interstate, and hard-sided restraint detail in this app is:
choices: Incomplete. Check with your manager where a page says it is a gap
Finished for every truck
Replaced by the Master Code, which is the law
quiz.why: Those pages state the points that were checked against an official source, and they mark the rest as gaps. The Master Code is not the law. Check with your manager where a page says something is a gap.

quiz.prompt: On Standard Hours, what is the most work for a solo driver in any 24 hours, and what rest goes with it?
choices: 12 hours work and 7 continuous hours stationary rest
14 hours work and 7 hours rest
10 hours work and no set rest
As long as you feel fine
quiz.why: That is the Standard Hours solo line for 24 hours on the NHVR work and rest hours page. 14 hours is a BFM figure, and only if you are actually on BFM.

quiz.prompt: In any 5½ hours on Standard Hours, a solo driver must:
choices: Work no more than 5¼ hours and take at least 15 continuous minutes rest
Keep working if the drop is close
Take 30 minutes only
Skip rest if the freight is milk
quiz.why: That is the first line of the Standard Hours solo table.

quiz.prompt: You are inside the hours and you are drowsy. What applies from 1 August 2026?
choices: You must not drive a heavy vehicle over 4.5 tonnes while impaired by fatigue or unfit, even inside the hours
The table is a target, so keep going
Only BFM drivers have to stop
A coffee resets the count
quiz.why: The NHVR work and rest page says the limits are outer limits and that the unfit-to-drive rule applies even inside them.

quiz.prompt: BFM’s 14 hours of work in 24 hours applies when:
choices: The office has confirmed you are operating under BFM, and that accreditation is still current
Every Monaro driver, every day
The customer is waiting
You feel fresh
quiz.why: BFM was an NHVAS module. Holders may continue until the accreditation expires, is cancelled, or they move to Heavy Vehicle Accreditation. Do not assume Monaro is on it.

quiz.prompt: Where are AFM work and rest hours written?
choices: On the operator’s AFM accreditation certificate, which the driver must carry
In this app, as a second Standard Hours table
On the customer order
They are the same as Standard Hours
quiz.why: The NHVR says AFM hours are on the certificate. This app does not copy a certificate we have not seen.

quiz.prompt: Can a driver pick Alternative Compliance Hours for themselves?
choices: No. The operator must hold ACA–Fatigue, and the hours are on that certificate
Yes, each morning
Yes, if the run is interstate
Yes, if Tanda says so
quiz.why: The NHVR says drivers cannot self-select Alternative Compliance Hours.

quiz.prompt: A night rest break on Standard Hours is:
choices: 7 continuous hours stationary rest between 10pm and 8am in the time zone of the driver’s base, or 24 continuous hours stationary rest
Any hour parked with the engine on
A break in the seat
Only a break taken in Victoria
quiz.why: That is the night-rest note under the Standard Hours solo table.

quiz.prompt: Stationary rest means:
choices: Time out of the fatigue-regulated heavy vehicle, or in an approved sleeper of a stationary vehicle
Waiting in the queue with the job still on
Loading, if you are sitting down
Driving under 80 km/h
quiz.why: That is the NHVR definition on the work and rest hours page. Loading and queue time are not described there as rest.

quiz.prompt: How many hours options can you operate under at once?
choices: One
Two, if you take the higher number
Standard Hours plus BFM
As many as the customer needs
quiz.why: The NHVR says you must only operate under one option at a time.

quiz.prompt: Under Standard Hours, when must you use a work diary?
choices: When you will work more than 100 km from your base
Only on trips the customer calls interstate
Never, if you use a run sheet for a 100 km-plus day
Only if you feel tired
quiz.why: That is the NHVR work diary page. You must also carry the diary if you did 100 km-plus Standard Hours work in the last 28 days. Inside 100 km you still need a local area record.

quiz.prompt: You did 100 km-plus work on Standard Hours last week. Today is a local day. The diary:
choices: Must still be carried, because that 100 km-plus work was in the last 28 days
Can stay in the office
Is cancelled
Is only for BFM
quiz.why: The record-keeping page says you must carry a work diary if you completed 100 km-plus Standard Hours work in the last 28 days.

quiz.prompt: Inside 100 km on Standard Hours, what record do you still need?
choices: A local area record, given to the record keeper
Nothing
Only a photo of the truck
A PBS approval
quiz.why: Local work is not ‘no record’. The NHVR requires a local area record.

quiz.prompt: How long must the record keeper keep fatigue records?
choices: Three years after they are created
28 days
Until the next toolbox talk
Seven business days
quiz.why: The record-keeping page says the records are kept for three years, in a readable form an authorised officer can access.

quiz.prompt: Your written diary is stolen. What is the first timing rule?
choices: Tell the NHVR within two business days, and use a supplementary record
Wait until you are back in Cooma next month
Rewrite yesterday from memory and say nothing
Stop keeping records
quiz.why: The work diary page says notify the NHVR within two business days if the diary is completed, lost, stolen or destroyed, and use a supplementary record.

quiz.prompt: How long may you rely on a supplementary record while you get a new written diary?
choices: A maximum of seven business days
28 days with no new diary
As long as the run sheet lasts
Until the accreditation expires
quiz.why: The work diary page says you may only use a supplementary record for a maximum of seven business days, and you must have a replacement by the end of that period.

quiz.prompt: Logmaster stops recording mid-shift. What do you do?
choices: Tell your manager straight away and use a supplementary record. Do not invent the missing hours
Keep driving and fill it in next week
Delete the day
Switch to no record because the screen is off
quiz.why: The NHVR record-keeper guide says a driver tells the record keeper, and the record keeper directs a supplementary record and notifies the NHVR within two business days.

choices: 21 days of that work day
Three years
The next depot barbecue
Seven business days, and not before

21.0 tonnes
Whatever fits on the deck

20.0 tonnes
25 tonnes if the pallets look even
Unlimited on air suspension

6.0 tonnes
17.0 tonnes
The same as a tri-axle

6.5 tonnes without checking
No steer limit

The general mass limit
The customer’s booking
The height of the pallets

20 metres
19 metres for every rigid
As long as the body

Every semi is now 20 metres with no other check
Only if it is a tanker
Only in Victoria

5 metres
Whatever the door will close on

quiz.prompt: You are 0.4 tonnes over the maximum mass. Roughly where does that sit?
choices: It can still be a minor breach. Substantial starts at the higher of 105% or 0.5 tonnes over
It is always severe
Under 1 tonne does not count
Only the driver can be wrong
quiz.why: The NHVR breach page: substantial starts at the higher of 105% of the maximum, rounded up to 0.1 t, or 0.5 t. Severe starts at 120%.

On every pallet, even a blocked one
Only for tankers
Only on the Monaro Highway
quiz.why: The performance standards page says 0.2 g upwards if relying on friction to withstand the force in the other directions. This fleet does not run tankers.

choices: Up to 200 mm front to back and up to 100 mm side to side
One metre is fine
No gap limit
Gaps only matter for curtains

choices: Re-block or re-strap before you move again
Leave it until Cooma
Open the doors on the highway to check
Add freight at the next shop without looking
quiz.why: The performance standards apply for the journey. A part-load that can become dislodged is not restrained.

choices: Is not the restraint. The 2018 guide says rope does not have the lashing capacity for a heavy load
Is enough if it looks tight
Replaces a rated side
Is required on every milk pallet
quiz.why: Load Restraint Guide 2018, general freight: do not use rope to restrain heavy loads.

quiz.prompt: A contained load may move a little up and down when:
choices: It is restrained horizontally, stability and weight distribution are not affected, and it does not become dislodged
The doors are open
You have not looked
The body is a tanker
quiz.why: That example is on the NHVR performance standards page. It is not permission for the load to walk out of the body.

The legal speed
Only for cars
Optional in the wet

Section 26E

The Master Code

Sends invoices

Fine if the driver agrees
Only a problem in Western Australia

The same as a Category 1 corporate penalty

Any road a rigid can use
Any mass you can fit

Last week’s load

Resets the 12 hours

Victorian time only

The same as a trip to Victoria
Illegal for milk
Allowed with no diary

choices: May continue until it expires, is cancelled, or the operator moves to Heavy Vehicle Accreditation
Ended for everyone on 1 August 2026
Became automatic for every operator for three years
Replaced Standard Hours for every driver

choices: 17.0 tonnes
16.5 tonnes
20.0 tonnes
9.0 tonnes

choices: Is still not the law. It can be evidence of what is reasonably practicable

Is optional only if you are accredited
Sets the penalty amounts

quiz.prompt: A loaded truck is waiting and the driver’s rest is about to start. What do you do?

Unload through the rest so the milk stays cold
Tell the driver to make the time up on the highway
quiz.why: Scheduling loading or unloading during a rest is a fatigue pressure the NHVR gives as an example under section 26E. A person who receives the goods can be a consignee. Change the plan. Do not push the driver to recover the time by speeding.
